clue.text: A drink of claret is an exception

indicators.note: 'of' here means the drink is taken out of the following run of words, letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A wine lover notes that claret is an exception among the drinks on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'claret is an exception', starting with the T of claret.
explanation.definitionFit: A herbal infusion such as camomile tea is a drink, so the general term defines it.

clue.text: Terriers repeatedly see you

indicators.note: repeatedly tells you to write the piece for terriers twice over

parts.note: Terriers is slang for the Territorial Army, abbreviated TA

explanation.surface: Someone sees off their dogs, the terriers, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army is Britain's reserve force of part-time soldiers, nicknamed the Terriers.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are casual British ways of saying goodbye, so the informal farewell is a synonym.

clue.text: Vegetable everyone put in picture

indicators.note: put in tells you one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a picture can be a shot, as in a photograph
everyone means all

explanation.surface: A photographer wants every person included in the photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A small onion relative used in cooking is a vegetable, so this is an example of the class.

clue.text: Sweet piece of meat

definitions.meaning: a sweet is a hazelnut chocolate or confection of that name
a small round boneless cut of lamb or pork bears the same name

explanation.surface: A menu item that is a dessert or a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for hazelnut names both a nutty sweet and a small round cut of lamb.

clue.text: European seen by Mark O'Hara

parts.note: a mark can be a scar
a Lett is a native of Latvia, so a European

explanation.surface: A European is spotted by someone called Mark O'Hara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark O'Hara' reads as a man's full name, but Mark gives SCAR and O'Hara is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Mitchell's heroine in Gone with the Wind is named Scarlett O'Hara, so her surname points to her first name.

clue.text: Bird had short tower for popular event

parts.note: a crow is a bird
had shortened is 'd, as in I'd
a tower here is one who tows, so a puller

explanation.surface: A bird once owned a stubby tower, used for a well-attended event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tower' is not a tall building but someone who tows, a puller.
explanation.definitionFit: An attraction that draws big audiences is a popular event, a synonym of the hyphenated term.

clue.text: 1 down after voyager finally sends message

indicators.note: after puts the farewell word behind the letter from voyager
finally picks the closing letter of the word voyager

parts.note: 1 down means goodbye, and adios is Spanish for goodbye

explanation.surface: A voyager signs off a message with a goodbye at the end of the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a signal by wireless is to send a message, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Look at pupil's place

definitions.meaning: to look at something closely is to stare it over
the pupil of the eye sits in the eye's globe

explanation.surface: A teacher looks over where a schoolchild sits.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to stare at; as a noun it is the globe of the eye, where the pupil sits.

clue.text: Loads you found on beach?

parts.note: thou is an old word for you
a beach is made of sands

explanation.surface: Wondering whether loads of things were found by you on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the playful picture: grains of sand beyond counting.
explanation.definitionFit: Loads, meaning a great many, matches the idiom for very large numbers.

clue.text: Distressing cutback Havana possibly rejected

parts.note: the back of the word cut is its last letter, T

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a Havana is an example of a cigar

explanation.surface: A distressing spending cutback means a Havana cigar must be turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutback' looks like one noun, but read it as 'cut back': the back letter of cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something distressing is sad and grievous, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: 1 down also led astray over and over again

parts.note: also means too

indicators.note: astray says the letters of led wander from their order

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
a second over gives another O

explanation.surface: Someone was led astray again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 down means a casual goodbye, which this jaunty British farewell also is.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated, jaunty British ways of saying goodbye, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Music, say, Orlando nearly composed for regiment

parts.note: the blues is a kind of music

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged
nearly drops the last letter of the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter Orlando nearly wrote music, such as the blues, for a regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: SAY and ORLAND are rearranged to make ANDROYALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Household Cavalry's second regiment bears this name, so a regiment is the class it belongs to.

clue.text: Elsewhere 21 came with cooked rice

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: cooked means messed about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone came elsewhere with a dish of cooked rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the German goodbye; 'elsewhere' points to its Italian equivalent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase for goodbye matches the German one at 21 used in another country.

clue.text: What Coleridge's wedding guest did with South American bones

definitions.note: plural, matching the singular name for a set of bones

parts.note: in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner the wedding guest met a tar, a sailor
US means American

explanation.surface: A quiz question about Coleridge's poem leads to South American bones.
explanation.walkthrough: Coleridge's poem has an old sailor stop a guest on his way to a wedding; a tar is a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The group of five long foot bones between the ankle and toes carries this collective anatomical name.

clue.text: Libertine in Slough or African city

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a slough is a bog or marsh
a libertine is a rake

explanation.surface: A libertine is to be found either in the English town of Slough or in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town west of London; here it is a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan city famed for its souks is an example of an African city.

clue.text: Info about large valley

indicators.note: about means going round, so the info piece wraps the letter

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Information about a large valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow Scottish valley is a type of valley, so this is a regional synonym.

clue.text: Preceding or following tear in pants

indicators.note: following places the word or after the rearranged letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, which tells you to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: Someone describes where a tear in their trousers is, before or after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers; in British slang it also means rubbish, here the anagram signal for TEAR IN, giving ANTERI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something situated before or in front is preceding, a synonym in position and time.

clue.text: Bloody allied soldiers

indicators.note: allied means joined together, so the two units of soldiers stand side by side

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers
RE is the Royal Engineers

explanation.surface: A bloody battle fought by Allied soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked so little it still shows blood is described as bloody, so the cooking term fits.

clue.text: Much ado in genuine case? No!

indicators.note: in tells you one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: genuine is real, which forms the case round the other piece

indicators.note: much of means most of, so the word for ado loses its last letter

parts.note: ado means fuss

explanation.surface: A real case causing much ado meets a flat no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Much' means 'much of', dropping the last S from FUSS to leave FUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no is a denial or rejection, so the exclamation stands for the noun.

clue.text: Left with an unfinished game after Gardner falls

indicators.note: after puts the other pieces behind the actress's name

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood actress

indicators.note: unfinished means the game's word loses its last letter

parts.note: chess is a game

explanation.surface: Ava Gardner falls, left with an unfinished game.
explanation.definitionFit: Masses of snow sliding down a mountain are falls, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Attending to empty house, say, without commotion

indicators.note: empty leaves only the outside letters of house
without means outside, so the example piece goes round the noise

parts.note: eg (for example) means say
din means commotion

explanation.surface: Someone attending to an empty house, without any fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking', so it is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heeding is paying attention to, so attending to is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Name one silly billy or another

definitions.note: means another silly billy, a fool

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a twit is a silly billy

explanation.surface: Someone names a silly billy, or perhaps another one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'silly billy': the answer is another fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool is another kind of idiot, so the answer stands for one further silly person.

clue.text: We freshen adieu in translation

indicators.note: in translation says the words are turned into something else, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: We give the French word for goodbye a fresh rendering in another language.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the anagram and also describes the German farewell as a new version of adieu.
explanation.definitionFit: The German phrase for goodbye is a translation of the French farewell.

clue.text: 1 down or 10 for Caesar's low land

definitions.meaning: the Latin word for farewell, said by a Roman

explanation.surface: A Roman general bids farewell to a low-lying region.
explanation.definitionFit: It is Latin for farewell and also a poetic word for a valley.

clue.text: Was trade diverted to the Land of the Rising Sun?

definitions.text: to the Land of the Rising Sun?

indicators.note: diverted means turned aside, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question whether commerce was rerouted towards Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Land of the Rising Sun is Japan; the question mark marks Japan as just one example of the general direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Going towards where the sun rises is heading in the direction of the dawn, an example of the term.

clue.text: Soviet leader's first name for it during Allied withdrawal

indicators.note: during says one piece sits inside the other
withdrawal means pulling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: allied means akin, related

explanation.surface: A Soviet leader's name is chosen at the time of an Allied pullout.
explanation.walkthrough: Khrushchev, Soviet leader 1953 to 1964, had this first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Khrushchev's forename is the Russian given name, so the description names it.

clue.text: Composer oddly overlooked Delian cow

parts.note: Gustav Holst was an English composer

indicators.note: oddly overlooked means skipping the odd-numbered letters and keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: A composer passes over a cow associated with Delius.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white dairy breed is a type of cow, so the example matches.

clue.text: André Gide initially appears in quiet street in French capital

parts.note: P is the music abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: appears in places the initials inside the French word

parts.note: rue is French for street

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of each name

explanation.surface: The novelist André Gide is seen on a quiet street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French capital' looks like Paris, but 'in French' gives RUE and only 'capital' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The Czech city is the capital of its country, so it is an example of a capital.
